title: Tree to Text and Back
statement:
You need to save a binary tree as one string and later rebuild it from that string alone, like storing a component tree in localStorage. Design two functions:

  • serialize(root) turns the tree into a single string, in any format you like.
  • deserialize(data) gets only that string and must rebuild a tree with exactly the same shape and values.

Values may be negative and may repeat, and the tree may be empty.

How it is tested. The runner calls one function, so implement roundTrip(root): write serialize and deserialize as helpers inside it and return deserialize(serialize(root)). A test passes when the returned tree equals the input tree. Returning root unchanged would also pass, so the tests cannot hold you to the rules; the exercise is the two helpers. deserialize must build new nodes using nothing except the string.

Trees are written in level order with null for a missing child.

examples.why: Values repeat, so they cannot tell you where a node goes, and -2 and 15 take several characters each. Separate tokens with a delimiter and store the shape explicitly.
Listing only the values gives "1,2" for this tree and for [1, 2] alike. The string must also record the missing children.
The empty tree needs an encoding of its own, and deserialize must turn it back into no tree at all.

constraints: The tree is at most 500 levels deep
deserialize may only use the string returned by serialize
hints: Values alone cannot describe a shape: many trees share the same preorder. What extra thing must the string record?
Write a marker such as # for every missing child. A preorder walk with markers ("node, left, right") then describes exactly one tree.
To read it back, split on your delimiter and consume tokens left to right with one shared index: a # means null; a number makes a node whose left subtree is read next, then its right.

explain.intuition:
A list of values loses the shape, because many trees have the same values in the same order. The fix is to write down the gaps too. Do a preorder walk and emit a value for every node and a marker like # for every missing child: [1, null, 2] becomes 1,#,2,#,#. Now the string has exactly one reading. Separate tokens with a delimiter, so that multi-digit and negative values like -456 stay one token.

Reading it back mirrors the writing. Preorder means "node, then its whole left subtree, then its whole right subtree", so a recursive reader with one shared position does the same: take a token; if it is #, return null; otherwise make a node, read its left subtree, then its right. The level-order format used on this page works too: write values row by row with markers, and rebuild with a queue that hands out children to parents in order. It is the same idea as JSON.stringify for a nested object: structure and data go into one string together.
steps: serialize: preorder walk; push the value for a node, # for null; join with commas.
deserialize: split the string on commas and keep an index i = 0.
read(): take tokens[i++]. If it is #, return null.
Otherwise make a node with that number, then set node.left = read() and node.right = read(), in that order.
The empty tree serializes to "#" and reads back as null.
pitfalls: Leaving out the null markers. The second example and [1, 2] then produce the same string.
Reading the string one character at a time. -2 and 15 are several characters each; split on a delimiter instead.
Placing nodes by value, as if the tree were a search tree, or looking values up in a map. Values can repeat, as in the first example.

solutions.title: Preorder with null markers
solutions.idea: Write node, left, right with # for every missing child. Read it back recursively with one shared position.

solutions.title: Level order with a queue
solutions.idea: Write the tree row by row with # for missing children. Rebuild with a queue: each parent takes the next two tokens as its children.

followups: Make the string shorter: which markers can you drop at the end, and what else could you compress?
If the tree were a search tree with distinct values, why would preorder values alone be enough, with no markers?
